## October 10 Results: Clean Sweep

You know, in my years covering this game, there's something deeply satisfying about watching the model click into gear when the postseason lights come on. We went 1-0 yesterday with a perfect read on the Guardians, and honestly, it felt like one of those picks where the numbers and the gut aligned beautifully.

The Sox-Guardians game played out exactly as we projected—Cleveland's home-field advantage and superior bullpen depth made the 53% confidence feel almost conservative in hindsight.

## October 11 Preview: Brewers Hosting the Dodgers

Now here's where it gets interesting. Tomorrow's top pick has us backing the Brewers at home against the Dodgers at 61% confidence—and the pitching matchup is absolutely fascinating.

Tarik Skubal taking the ball for LA is no joke. The guy's been dominant, and in most scenarios, you'd lean heavily toward any team he's starting for. But here's what I've learned over the decades: October baseball is a different animal, and American Family Field in Milwaukee has a way of neutralizing even the most elite arms.

Jacob Misiorowski gets the nod for Milwaukee, and while he doesn't have Skubal's pedigree, the home crowd and the Brewers' ability to manufacture runs in tight games give them an edge the model likes.

## The Veteran's Take

I've seen plenty of regular season aces struggle in their first October starts—the adrenaline, the tighter strike zones, the playoff-caliber lineups that don't chase. Skubal will be fine long-term, but this particular spot? The Brewers have the pieces to scratch across enough runs.

The 61% confidence tells you this isn't a slam dunk. It's a lean, backed by situational analysis and home-field metrics that historically favor Milwaukee in these pitching duels. That's playoff baseball—margins are thin, and you take your edges where you find them.

Let's see if we can make it 2-0 heading into the weekend.
